acceptance: After an oracle SHIP review, or after a stand-in, the pull request merges with no manual rerun, or after one documented action (shown on a real or test pull request). The action is not a rerun of each earlier failing run.

Either the check is reported once per head (later runs supersede earlier ones), or runs that fail while waiting for the oracle no longer leave a failing check run on the head, without a job-level `if:` skip on the required check.
Replying to several review threads starts at most one oracle-review evaluation, or the decision to keep the `pull_request_review` trigger is recorded with the reason.
An oracle App review and a dismissal re-evaluate the required check. A stand-in has a stated one-step path to re-evaluate (test or recorded run).
docs/operations/soundness-drain.md:30-32 states the recovery that actually works.
A test or recorded CI evidence covers the stale-failure case.
description:
Every `oracle-review` run that fails while it waits for the oracle's review stays on the head as a failed check run. After the oracle posts a SHIP review, or after a stand-in, the pull request stays BLOCKED until each earlier failing run is rerun by hand. A passing run next to a failing one does not clear the failure.

Two kinds of run leave a failure:
- The `pull_request` run started by a push, which fails while no oracle review exists yet. This is the common case. #2843 (head 3fe4971b0) has `pull_request` run 37982501043, which needed attempt 2, and `pull_request_review` run 37982952354. #2820 run 37941585023 also needed attempt 2.
- `pull_request_review` runs (submitted or dismissed) started by thread replies and other review events, before the stand-in existed. On #2784 (head 8eb562e01) a fresh `pull_request` run succeeded after the stand-in, yet the pull request stayed BLOCKED. #2769 showed the same.

Reruns must be done one at a time, because parallel `gh run rerun` calls cancel each other through the `oracle-review-<pr>` concurrency group (.github/workflows/oracle-review.yml:24-26). The documented recovery (close and reopen) is not enough on its own and restarts the whole CI suite. docs/operations/soundness-drain.md:30-32 says to rerun "the latest oracle-review run". That is wrong: each earlier failing run must be rerun.

Absorbed from oracle-review-thread-reply-run-churn-20261008: `oracle-review.yml` triggers on `pull_request_review: [submitted, dismissed]`. A reply in a review thread is a submitted review, so replying to N threads starts N runs. Concurrency cancels all but the last, but each run still takes a runner slot. Since 2026-10-08 there have been 170 review-event runs (62 success, 51 failure, 57 cancelled). A possible shared fix is to drop the `pull_request_review` trigger and re-evaluate by `workflow_dispatch` after the oracle posts its review. That fix must keep the required check re-evaluating when the oracle App posts a review and when it dismisses one.

Guardrails:
- Do not add a job-level `if:` skip to the required `oracle-review` check. A skipped required check counts as passing.
- Do not weaken the required check, its stand-in rule or the soundness path list.
- Stand-ins are issue comments and never re-evaluate the check automatically, so they need a stated one-step path.
